items.text: None of ContentManager's three constructors rejects a null IServiceProvider, whereas XNA's constructors throw ArgumentNullException. CNA relies on this on purpose: standalone managers in tools and CNA's own tests are built as ContentManager(nullptr, root) and receive their device through setGraphicsDevice. This is a documented deviation (stated on the ContentManager resolution-rules deep dive), not a defect.

The XNB DateTimeReader masks off and discards the two DateTimeKind bits and keeps only the 62-bit tick count, because sharp-runtime's System::DateTime does not store a kind. A DateTime written as Utc or Local loads as a plain tick value. The header documents this as a deliberate deviation.
items.evidence: modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/Xnb/DecimalDateTimeContentTypeReaders.hpp (DateTimeReader, kindMask and 'Deviation: DateTimeKind is parsed but discarded')

items.text: MorphTargetDataEXT::Stride's doc comment says the stride is 'any of CLAUDE.md's stride table', but CNA's CLAUDE.md has no stride table (zero occurrences of 'stride'). The canonical table is VertexDeclarationFidelity.hpp. This is source-comment drift only; GltfImportCore.hpp, which had the same reference, no longer carries it.

The comment on the one-argument BuildSkeleton(skin, unitScale) says every root joint keeps an identity prefix. The code it delegates to does not do that. Because no parent can be found in the empty scene graph it passes, a root joint that has a parent node takes the cgltf_node_transform_world fallback and still receives the ancestry term. Only the mesh-node cancellation (identity mesh-node transform) and the scene-node mappings are missing. Production loaders use the scene-aware overload. The one-argument form is called only by test oracles that need palette order, so this is comment drift, not a behaviour defect.
